transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-12
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 55m
Attendees: Aisha Patel (Redwood AE), Rajiv Menon (Redwood SE), Elena Ruiz (NovaQuill Head of ML), Marcus Hale (NovaQuill Platform Eng), Priya Anand (CTO)
Recording link: https://redwood.example.com/meet/ff-20270112-nq-01 (internal)

Auto-summary (auto): Quick Optimize console demo, cost tradeoffs between prefetch/prefix KV vs session affinity cache, batching/sim, next steps to run pilot

[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Elena: yes loud and clear, thanks Aisha. we got Marcus and Priya on as well.
[00:10] Marcus: hi all, audio is good.
[00:12] Aisha: perfect, quick agenda - we'll walk through the Optimize console econ sim, show a prefetch(prefix)/KV demo, then contrast with sessionization affinity caching and batching tradeoffs, then Q&A and next steps. sound good?
[00:22] Priya: yep sounds great.
[00:25] Rajiv: jumping in on the demo side — we'll also show an autoscale + batch profile that keeps p95 under 250ms for short prompts.
[00:33] Elena: our primary goal is to cut token cost by 40-60% without pushing latency above 300ms for our chat flows.
[00:41] Aisha: got it. Marcus, want to quickly share your stack and traffic shape?
[00:44] Marcus: sure yeah we've got user chat across web and mobile. 75% of interactions are short Q/A (tokens ~12-40), 25% are longer multi-turn session threads. baseline is about 600 qps peak, with spiky bursts to 1200 qps. host on GCP. retention reqs: 30 days for audit logs, and we need SSO via SAML.
[01:08] Aisha: cool — that helps. we'll map that to prefetch assumptions.
[01:12] Rajiv: ok sharing my screen, Optimize console -> "Economics" -> "Simulate", you should see the prefetch slider and a combination view. note: our default sim uses prefix length 128 tokens, kv hit rate assumption 35% for these short prompts, and batching window 12ms.
[01:36] Elena: i see, that 35% is that empirical or default?
[01:40] Rajiv: it's conservative default; you'd replace it with a real measured hit-rate once we run a warmup. for your workload the short prompts actually help because prefixes are repeated. but multi-turn threads complicate it.
[01:52] Marcus: question — what's the difference between "prefix prefetch" and "session cache" in your console?
[01:56] Rajiv: good — prefix prefetch populates KV entries for common initial tokens or system prompts so when a new request arrives it's more likely to hit the KV, saving decoding costs. session cache binds KV entries to a session id and tends to keep larger context per session — better for long-lived conversations but increases working set and memory pressure.
[02:20] Priya: so session cache has higher memory but better hit for multi-turn long sessions, prefix is lower memory and helps the short queries?
[02:26] Rajiv: exactly. also prefix prefetch pairs well with micro-batching because short queries batch nicely. session affinity makes batching trickier since you need to preserve context locality.
[02:40] Elena: can you run a side-by-side sim for our 600 qps baseline vs a 1200 qps burst scenario?
[02:45] Rajiv: yep will switch scenarios. switching to NovaQuill sample template — loading... ok baseline 600 qps, batch size target 4 to 8, concurrency 32. when prefetch at 40% hit-rate, cost reduction shows ~47% tokens per second savings in the sim. with session cache (keep-alive 300s) the sim shows ~30% savings but requires 3x more KV memory.
[03:12] Marcus: 3x memory — do you mean GPU memory or KV store memory?
[03:16] Rajiv: KV store / host memory for the cache metadata, and some model-side KV allocations. GPU working set can grow slightly because of pinned KV pages, but most impact is in RAM.
[03:26] Elena: any latency tradeoffs?
[03:28] Rajiv: prefix prefetch keeps median latency roughly the same or slightly better due to fewer decode steps; session cache can reduce decode tokens but may increase tail latency during cache rehydration or if the cache misses and you have to fetch a bigger context.
[03:44] Aisha: real-world tip — we often recommend hybrid: use prefix prefetch for common system prompts and session cache only for authenticated heavy users with >3 turns. that usually gives 50-60% cost reduction while keeping p95 under target.
[03:58] Priya: hybrid makes sense. what's the ops complexity?
[04:02] Rajiv: complexity is mostly around eviction and TTLs, and required instrumentation. the console has TTL heatmaps and we produce recommended eviction policies based on lookups per minute.
[04:12] Elena: walk me through the econ model assumptions — where do your cost numbers come from?
[04:17] Rajiv: we use per-token cost estimates tied to model family and quantization profile, plus infra unit cost — CPU/GPU time per decoding token, KV lookup cost per 100k ops, plus a small storage and egress factor. we expose those line items so you can tweak them.
[04:34] Elena: can I plug in our cloud costs?
[04:36] Aisha: yes — in the sim you can set your cloud provider egress and storage rates; we'll send a CSV that plugs your GCP node pricing so the numbers line up.
[04:44] Marcus: about batching — you mentioned continuous batching vs fixed windows, which does Optimize favor?
[04:49] Rajiv: we prefer continuous batching with an adaptive window that expands under low load and collapses when latency targets get tight. you can set a max latency budget and the runtime will prioritize latency vs throughput. in the console sim we surface the effective batch size distribution so you can see how often batches are 1,2,4,8,16.
[05:10] Elena: show us the batch distribution for the burst scenario.
[05:12] Rajiv: switching. during the 1200 qps burst with our config, median batch size moves from 6 to 10, but tail remains small because we cap the wait time at 18ms. that's why p95 stays near 280ms in our sim.
[05:28] Priya: interesting — and what about fallback policies if prefetch model variant isn't available?
[05:33] Rajiv: we have automatic fallback to a lower-capacity compatible variant or routed region; you can prioritize cost tiers. console shows simulated fallback events and estimated cost delta.
[05:42] Marcus: any caveats around tokenization differences? our prompts have some non-ascii and embeddings mixed in.
[05:48] Rajiv: tokenization affects prefix matching — non-ascii can fragment tokens so hit rates drop. we recommend normalizing or canonicalizing system prompts and running a small tokenizer analysis (we can help with a script) to estimate realistic hit-rates.
[06:02] Elena: do you have a quick example for our traffic?
[06:04] Rajiv: yes i uploaded a 7-day sample sim into the console earlier — i'm switching to that. best to look at the prefix heatmap... see these top 12 prefixes? about 18% of requests start with just three tokens that are identical. that's a strong signal for prefetch.
[06:22] Priya: ok that explains it. what's the expected engineering lift to instrument the session id and keys?
[06:27] Marcus: i can take that but curious how Redwood expects the session binding — cookie vs auth token?
[06:32] Rajiv: session id can be any stable identifier you supply in the API call. we recommend a short opaque session token, rotated per-login if needed. the SDK supports session header X-Session-ID. minimal code change — one extra header per call.
[06:44] Aisha: i can share our snippet and a small middleware for node/python that injects X-Session-ID.
[06:49] Elena: great.
[06:51] Rajiv: switching to the "cost compare" heatmap — left side is no prefetch, middle is prefix prefetch, right is session affinity. notice the token throughput and also the effective token cost line item. with prefix prefetch your decode tokens drop 40% and the prefetch storage cost is minimal. with session affinity decode drop 55% but storage and eviction ops increase and you need a higher mem tier.
[07:18] Marcus: what's the breakeven point for prefetch storage vs decode cost?
[07:22] Rajiv: it depends on hit-rate. in our sim for NovaQuill, at a 20% hit-rate breakeven is around 350 qps. above that prefetch pays off. at 40% it's clearly dominant.
[07:33] Priya: can the sim export to CSV? we want to run with our finance model.
[07:36] Rajiv: yes exportable — you'll get per-line items for decode tokens, kv ops, storage, gpu-minutes, and an assumed hourly infra cost. we'll attach the CSV.
[07:45] Aisha: action: we'll send that CSV with the NovaQuill-adjusted GCP pricing.
[07:49] Elena: great. any security concerns with storing prefixes? that's sensitive chat prompts.
[07:55] Rajiv: good call — we treat KV entries as ephemeral by default; they can be encrypted using your KMS in Private or Dedicated. for hosted we support envelope encryption and RBAC scoping. we also do audit logs and can redaction policies for PII.
[08:12] Marcus: need SOC 2 details — we'll want the security pack.
[08:15] Aisha: noted, we'll attach SOC 2 docs and the security whitepaper.
[08:20] Rajiv: back to sim — now i'm toggling a conservative TTL and LRU eviction: you'll see the hit-rate drops slowly after 2h without access. if you have heavy reuse within sessions, increase the TTL for those session keys only.
[08:34] Elena: what about the tradeoff between TTL and eviction ops cost?
[08:37] Rajiv: longer TTL = fewer KV writes but more memory; eviction ops are proportional to churn. if you have lots of ephemeral sessions, churn can blow up ops cost. console shows ops per minute to help tune it.
[08:50] Priya: can Redwood run a small POC where we route 10% of traffic through prefix prefetch and measure live delta?
[08:55] Rajiv: absolutely — we recommend a canary 10-20% with canary metrics preconfigured in the console. we can provide a rollout policy and alerts for latency regressions.
[09:06] Marcus: timeline? how fast could we start?
[09:09] Aisha: if we get sample logs today we can produce the econ sim + config in 48-72 hours. then pilot kickoff week of Jan 18 as discussed.
[09:18] Elena: ok sending logs by Monday.
[09:21] Rajiv: quick note — for the pilot we suggest targeting only web short queries first to maximize hit-rate. after that we expand to session users.
[09:29] Aisha: question for Priya — what's your approval process for a pilot that touches customer data?
[09:33] Priya: our legal wants DPA and a short security review; engineering needs a non-prod staging test. should be fine with those.
[09:40] Aisha: we'll include DPA and security checklist in the packet.
[09:43] Elena: a couple of clarifying questions — you mentioned tokenizer scripts; can you run a quick tokenization pass on a 1k sample while we're on the call?
[09:51] Rajiv: yes i have a small script. uploading results... okay for this sample the effective token overlap for our top prefixes was 36% not 18 that i showed earlier — the prefetch upside just improved.
[10:05] Marcus: nice. that bumps the sim numbers?
[10:07] Rajiv: with 36% hit-rate the simulated cost reduction for prefix prefetch jumps to ~55% for short prompt mix.
[10:12] Priya: are there any model-level changes we need to make? quantization or smaller variant?
[10:16] Rajiv: you can pair prefetch with a quantized variant for lower per-token cost; Optimize suggests a variant based on sequence length distribution. we can show that in the console. keep in mind quality tradeoffs for long-form responses.
[10:30] Elena: ok let's talk about observability — what dashboards do you provide during pilot?
[10:34] Rajiv: we provide per-route token breakdown, KV hit/miss rates, batch size distribution, and latency percentiles. alerts for p95 regressions and fallback events.
[10:44] Aisha: we'll set up a shared dashboard link and invite your team.
[10:47] Marcus: perfect. any cost for the console features?
[10:50] Aisha: console Optimize is included in enterprise packages; pilot analytics are complimentary for the first trial period. we'll confirm in the email.
[10:59] Elena: last question — does Redwood handle multi-region consistency for KV? we're global and need low lat for EU and NA.
[11:05] Rajiv: we offer regional KV clusters with eventual consistency and optional synchronous replication for critical keys — that has higher latency and cost. console sim includes region routing cost lines.
[11:18] Priya: thanks.
[11:20] Aisha: ok recap: Redwood sends econ CSV + SOC2 + security pack + code snip and middleware; NovaQuill sends sample logs and confirms pilot date; SE to prepare config snippet and pilot runbook.
[11:33] Elena: sounds good.
[11:35] Marcus: i'll drop the logs in the shared S3 link by Monday.
[11:38] Aisha: perfect, i'll follow up with calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.
[11:42] Rajiv: any other technical Qs?
[11:45] Priya: none here.
[11:47] Aisha: thanks everyone — we'll follow up.
